artworks.title: Iphis and Anaxarete
artworks.description: Solis’ Ovid woodcut names the Cypriot youth Iphis before hard-hearted Anaxarete — the inset Vertumnus tells Pomona. Carefully distinct from Cretan Iphis whom Isis transforms for Ianthe.

artworks.title: Iphis and Anaxarete
artworks.description: National Gallery of Victoria plate of the Metamorphoses tale: Iphis’ hopeless suit and Anaxarete’s scorn. Print culture kept the Cypriot lovers legible beside the more famous Cretan Iphis.

artworks.title: Anaxarete Turns to Stone at Iphis' Funeral
artworks.description: Krauss freezes Ovid’s climax: Anaxarete watches Iphis’ funeral pass and hardens into stone. The youth’s death is the moral engine of the Cypriot metamorphosis.

artworks.title: Death of Iphis
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum RP-P-2014-34-82: Iphis hanged — the humble lover Anaxarete mocked until Aphrodite’s revenge. Northern Ovid cycles made his suicide a stock warning against hard-heartedness.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses XIV (Iphis and Anaxarete)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Vertumnus’ cautionary tale to Pomona: Cypriot Iphis loves Anaxarete, hangs himself, and she turns to stone at his bier — not the Cretan Iphis of Book IX.
